free_tier.stated: 1 GiB stored data on the free tier; 50,000 document reads/day; 20,000 writes/day; 10 GiB/month outbound

egress.terms: Metered — 10 GiB/month outbound free, then GCP rates. 10 GiB/month = ~340 MB/day, 1,500x short of 500 GB/day.

tooling: Firebase Admin SDK, client SDKs, REST/gRPC API, `gcloud firestore export` to a bucket; documents are JSON-ish with a native `Bytes` type (no base64 bloat)
chaining: 1 GiB per database; 'Cloud Firestore allows exactly one free database per project'. 500 GB needs 500 projects, each with its own billing-less free quota and its own 10 GiB/month egress.
limits_note: 1 GiB total; 1 MiB per document; 1 MiB - 89 bytes per field value; 50K reads/day; 20K writes/day; 7.5 KiB max index entry; only ONE free database per project
reliability_note: Reliable; has a native Bytes type so no base64 overhead. The 20K writes/day cap means 1 GiB at 1 MiB/doc = 1,024 documents, which is trivially fine, but re-writing or migrating burns the quota. Single-field indexes add storage you do not control.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'Stored data | 1 GiB'; 'Outbound data transfer | 10 GiB per month'; 'Maximum size for a document | 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)'; 'Maximum size of a field value | 1 MiB - 89 bytes'
'Document reads 50,000 per day'; 'Document writes 20,000 per day'; 'Cloud Firestore allows exactly one free database per project'
arithmetic: 50,000 reads/day x 1 MiB max document = 52.4 GB/day of theoretical read — 10x short of 500 GB/day, and the 10 GiB/month egress cap cuts it to 340 MB/day
